scope: Local desktop connection admission only; no remote OpenWrt commands, algorithms, host identity or authentication semantics changed.
behavior: Startup retains conditional background firewall audit and rule creation; neither is required before a reachable SSH login.
Firewall audit and application allow rules are no longer login prerequisites.
The actual connected TCP socket is handed to Paramiko, without a second probe.
Only local access denial invokes deferred existing policy preparation, followed by one TCP retry.
Refusal, timeout, DNS errors, authentication failure and host key change do not invoke policy preparation.
Existing backup, native snapshot verification, preservation and rollback are retained.

findings_fixed: Wrapped NoValidConnectionsError has errno None; unwrap its errors to retain native access-denial code and show a non-secret actionable message.
If cancellation watcher Thread.start raises, close the established socket and never join an unstarted thread.
confirmed: No firewall audit or allow-rule prerequisite for a reachable interactive login.
Paramiko accepts an already connected sock and still validates host identity and authenticates.
Only an access-denial result can invoke existing policy preparation; one TCP retry; no authentication retry.
10013 alone does not identify the blocking policy or application.
Startup conditional audit is retained independently.

sources.supports: Connected sock reuse with normal host-key checks and authentication.
Wrapper errno None; actual errors are exposed via errors dict.
10013 WSAEACCES means permission denied, with more than one possible cause.
connect_ex returns native connection error code instead of raising for C connect errors.
Joining a thread before start raises RuntimeError.

additional_evidence: A real SSH login completes while the actual startup audit thread remains blocked on an Event.
A subsequent audit failure leaves that authenticated connection active.
Windows asynchronous exception completion reads SO_ERROR=10013, closes the first socket, requests repair once and returns the second socket.
Asynchronous success uses the original socket; SO_ERROR=10061 does not request policy repair.
Cancellation immediately after TCP denial prevents policy repair.

sources.supports: Nonblocking connect success appears in writefds; failure appears in exceptfds and requires getsockopt SO_ERROR.
Event.wait blocks until set; used to exercise actual concurrent audit and login without timer-based synchronization.
Explicit Windows Firewall block rules take precedence over conflicting allow rules; adding allow rules is not a universal unblock guarantee.

second_official_review.boundary: Windows local loopback SSH tested. Windows asynchronous failures injected through native socket API boundary. Customer application login, actual privileged policy mutation, and native Debian 12 runtime remain unverified.
